cues.en: Welcome. This is a series in which I am going to endeavor to put together pretty much all of my work. My name is John Ravecki. I'm an assistant professor at the University of Toronto. I'm in the psychology department and in the cognitive science program. And I also teach for the Buddhism Psychology and Mental Health program. I've produced a lot of videos on a lot of various topics. Some of you have perhaps seen them.
cues.zh: 欢迎大家。在这个系列中，我将尽力把我的几乎所有研究成果整合在一起。我叫 John Ravecki，是多伦多大学的助理教授。我任职于心理学系和认知科学项目，同时也在“佛教、心理学与心理健康”项目中任教。我曾围绕许多不同主题制作过很多视频，你们中有些人可能已经看过了。

cues.en: But what I want to do now in this series is draw it all together and present to you an overall unified argument that can show you the interconnections between pieces that you might have seen before. Now how all this got started is I got very interested in a particular phenomena. I got interested in the fact that there seemed to be a growing confluence between
cues.zh: 但现在在这个系列里，我想把所有内容融会贯通，向大家呈现一个整体而统一的论述，展示你们之前可能看过的各个部分之间的内在联系。这一切的缘起，是我对一种特定现象产生了浓厚的兴趣。我注意到，对佛教感兴趣的人群

cues.en: people who are interested in Buddhism and people who are interested in cognitive science. We'll talk a little bit later as we go on what cognitive science is. But you know some of this already in the world at large because we're going through what's called the mindfulness revolution. Mindfulness is being spoken of everywhere. I was in a bookstore yesterday, chapters, and there's a whole section just on mindfulness itself. So why is the mindfulness revolution occurring? Well, it's occurring particularly because of this intersection
cues.zh: 与对认知科学感兴趣的人群之间，似乎正在出现越来越多的交集。随着内容的推进，我们稍后会聊聊什么是认知科学。但放眼当今世界，大家多少已经了解一些了，因为我们正在经历所谓的“正念革命”。如今到处都在谈论正念。我昨天去了一家 Chapters 书店，那里甚至有一整片专区全都是关于正念的。那么，为什么会出现正念革命呢？它之所以出现，正是因为这种交叉融合

cues.en: between Buddhism and cognitive science. But why is this happening? And why is it, you know, so explosive in nature? And what do we mean by mindfulness? Some of the work I've done is trying to get clear about that. We're going to talk about that in this series. Now there's also a lot of other things that in my mind seem to be convergent with this growing confluence between Buddhism and cognitive science.
cues.zh: 在佛教与认知科学之间。但为什么会这样？又为什么会呈现出如此爆发式的增长？我们所说的正念究竟指什么？我做过的一些研究正是试图弄清这一点。我们将在本系列中探讨这些问题。此外，在我看来还有许多其他现象，正与佛教和认知科学之间这种日益深化的融合趋于一致。

cues.en: There is an increasing interest both academically and in the public at large in the topic of wisdom. Something that people did not talk about very much not that long ago. Well, wisdom is now a very hot topic within psychology and cognitive science. And books offering to train you in wisdom are, again, becoming popular. Same bookstore experience yesterday. I bought my son a book called How to Be a Stoic.
cues.zh: 无论是在学术界还是大众当中，人们对智慧这一话题的兴趣都日益浓厚。这在不久前还是大家很少谈论的东西。然而，如今智慧已成为心理学和认知科学领域的大热门。那些宣称能培养智慧的书籍，也再度风靡起来。昨天在书店就印证了这点，我给我儿子买了一本名叫《如何成为斯多葛主义者》的书。

cues.en: How is it that a philosophical position from the Hellenistic era has become a popular book that people are seeking? Why is there this hunger for wisdom? And why are people meeting it with these kinds of things? The stoicism, the philosophies of the Hellenistic period. We're going to talk about that. I think there's good reason for that.
cues.zh: 一个希腊化时期的哲学流派，怎么就变成了一本备受追捧的畅销书呢？为什么大家会对智慧如此饥渴？又为什么会用这些东西来填补空缺呢？比如斯多葛主义，以及希腊化时期的种种哲学。我们接下来就聊聊这个。我觉得这背后是有充分理由的。

cues.en: Of course, there's increasing academic and public interest in psychedelics. I just gave a talk earlier this week at Yale about psychedelics and the increasing interest in psychedelics and psychedelic experiences. You're seeing radical things with them. People can be released from treatment-resistant addiction. They can overcome post-traumatic stress disorder. Like the normal with the best therapy
cues.zh: 当然，学术界和公众对致幻剂的兴趣也越来越浓厚。我本周早些时候刚在耶鲁大学做了一场演讲，内容就是关于致幻剂，以及大家对致幻剂和迷幻体验日益增长的兴趣。你会发现它们带来了翻天覆地的改变。难治性成瘾的患者能借此摆脱依赖。创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）也能被克服。要知道，哪怕用上最好的常规疗法，

cues.en: Solution rate for people with post-traumatic stress disorder is about, if things go really well, 20% or so. You introduce psychedelics into the therapy and you can get the healing rate up to 80%. So what's going on there? Why is there this interest? There's an increasing public interest which is matched by a huge academic in the topics of happiness.
cues.zh: PTSD 患者的治愈率在一切顺利的情况下，也就大概 20% 左右。但如果把致幻剂引入治疗，治愈率可以直接提升到 80%。所以这背后到底是怎么回事？为什么会引发这种关注？公众对此的兴趣水涨船高，与此同时，学术界对幸福感这一课题也爆发出了巨大的研究热情。

cues.en: We've always been a happiness-oriented culture, life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness, and so forth. But it's taken a particularly interesting turn. The topic of meaning and meaning in life is coming to the fore. People in more and more are talking about not just sheer contentedness, but what it is for a human life to be meaningful. And it turns out that meaning in life is terrifically important.
cues.zh: 我们一直生活在一种以幸福为导向的文化中，生命、自由和对幸福的追求等等。但这正在发生一个特别有趣的转变。意义，以及生命意义的话题，正在走向前台。越来越多的人不再只谈论单纯的满足感，而是开始探讨人生怎样才算有意义。事实证明，生命的意义极其重要。

cues.en: It's very predictive of well-being. It's very predictive of how well you are doing in your life in general. So it is no wonder that our people are seeking it out. Now, my contention and what I'm going to argue is it's no coincidence that all of these things are happening right now. It's no coincidence. There's confluence between Buddhism, the mindfulness revolution, the interest in wisdom and ancient philosophies like Stoicism.
cues.zh: 它能极好地预测人的幸福感。它能极好地预测你整个人生过得究竟有多好。所以难怪大家都在追寻它。那么，我的观点也是我接下来要论证的，就是这一切在当下发生绝非巧合。佛教、正念革命、对智慧的关注，以及像斯多葛主义这样的古代哲学，它们交汇融合绝非偶然。

cues.en: the increasing public interest in psychedelics and transformative experiences and mystical experiences, right? The increasing academic and public interest in meaning in life. There's all a reason for it. There's a unifying account for why this is happening. But there's another set of things. This is sort of the light side of what I'm talking about. There's a set of dark factors that seem to be converging as well, right? We have...
cues.zh: 公众对致幻剂、转化性体验和神秘体验的兴趣与日俱增，对吧？学术界和大众对人生意义的关注也越来越多。这背后都是有原因的，这一切的发生都有一套统一的解释。但还有另一组现象。这算是我所谈内容的积极一面。与此同时，似乎也有一组消极因素在汇聚，对吧？我们面临着……

cues.en: What seems to be, although people are disputing it, but I think the evidence is becoming clearer and clearer. The CDC just released some data recently. We're going through a mental health crisis. Suicide is spiking, and it's, right? Now, there are some socioeconomic factors, but there's clearly other things that are at work. There's increasing sense, many people are expressing it, of losing touch with reality.
cues.zh: 似乎——尽管有人对此存在争议，但我认为证据已经越来越清晰了。CDC 最近刚刚发布了一些数据。我们正经历一场心理健康危机。自杀率正在激增，而且这种趋势，对吧？现在，固然存在一些社会经济因素，但显然还有其他因素在起作用。越来越多的人表达出一种脱离现实的无力感。

cues.en: We encounter more and more often in individuals and groups nihilism, expressions of cynicism, expressions of deep kinds of frustration and futility. You have the abandonment of trust in any of our public institutions. We're losing, right, we've completely lost any sort of faith or trust in our political system. We're losing faith in our judicial system, right.
cues.zh: 在个人和群体身上，我们越来越频繁地看到虚无主义、愤世嫉俗的流露，以及深深的挫败感与无力感。人们不再信任任何公共机构。我们正在丧失，没错，我们已经彻底丧失了对政治体制的任何信仰或信任。我们对司法系统的信任也正在动摇，对吧。

cues.en: Religious affiliation is declining consistently throughout people's participation in clubs, organization is in decline. In general, and my co-authors on the book, Zombies in Western Culture, The 21st Century Crisis, Chris Massipietro and Philip Misovich, we argued that
cues.zh: 宗教认同在持续下降，人们对俱乐部、各类组织的参与度也在走低。总的来说，我和《西方文化中的丧尸：21世纪的危机》这本书的合著者，Chris Massipietro 与 Philip Misovich，我们认为

cues.en: The sense of being out of touch has gone on with an increasing sense. And we'll talk about this, because I'm going to use this term technically. We're going to talk about this in Frankfurt's use of it. There's an increasing sense of more and more bullshit everywhere, pervading. And if you take a look at the book, we actually chart how this has been spiking. And it's concorded with all kinds of other increases in these dark factors.
cues.zh: 这种与现实脱节的感觉，伴随着一种愈发强烈的感受而不断蔓延。我们稍后会聊到这点，因为我是要在学术意义上使用这个词。我们会按照 Frankfurt 的用法来探讨它。人们越来越觉得，无处不在的“胡说八道”在四处弥漫。如果你翻开那本书，我们其实绘制了这种现象激增的走势图。而这与所有这些黑暗因素的各种增长，都是相吻合的。

cues.en: People are getting the sense that we're spending, and you can see this already in the public media, but it's also within the academic world, that we're spending too much time in our virtual environments. There seems to be increasing evidence, for example, of a connection between various social media, increased depression, increased loneliness.
cues.zh: 人们逐渐意识到我们在虚拟环境里花的时间太多了，你不仅能在大众媒体上看到这种讨论，学术界也同样如此。比如，越来越多的证据表明，各种社交媒体与抑郁、孤独感加剧之间存在着关联。

cues.en: And then more in general, and we'll talk about how this shows up a little bit more implicitly. It shows up in the entertainment we seek and the mythologies we like, like the zombies. We're gonna talk about that. Why are zombies so big? Why are superheroes so big right now? There's an increase, these mythological, and we'll talk about what myth means, these mythological forms, I'm gonna argue are expressions of a cultural sense, a sense that we're stuck somehow.
cues.zh: 更普遍的是，我们稍后会聊聊这在潜意识层面是如何体现的。它体现在我们追逐的娱乐和热衷的神话叙事中，比如丧尸文化。我们一会儿会谈谈这个。为什么丧尸题材这么火？为什么超级英雄现在这么流行？这种激增的现象，这些神话——稍后我们会讨论“神话”的定义——我认为这些神话形态，正是一种文化心理的宣泄，表达着我们似乎陷入某种困境的感觉。

cues.en: One way you can note that is just by noting how pervasive, almost to the point of being a constant factor in our background, is people talking about crisis and collapse. Apocalypse, the zombie apocalypse, the imminent collapse of civilization. All of these things are now pervasive. They're taken for granted. At one point, right, the
cues.zh: 大家留意一下就能发现，人们对危机和崩溃的谈论有多么普遍，几乎成了我们生活中挥之不去的背景音。世界末日、丧尸末日、文明即将崩溃。所有这些现在都随处可见。大家早已习以为常。曾几何时，展现这种场景的

cues.en: movies demonstrating this had to be sort of science fiction, they were considered radical, but now this is becoming a pervasive background sense. Now I think all of these negative factors also have a unifying explanation. In fact, what I'm going to argue throughout the course of this series is that the positive factors and the negative factors all point to a unified explanation.
cues.zh: 电影还属于某种科幻片，被视作激进前卫，但现在这已经变成了一种挥之不去的普遍氛围。现在我认为，所有这些消极因素背后，也存在一个统一的解释。事实上，我在本系列中要阐述的核心观点是：积极因素和消极因素，其实都指向同一个统一的解释。

cues.en: This is going to be an idea that our culture is experiencing a profound meaning crisis, a crisis in meaning. Now, we're going to have to talk about what does that meaning mean. Now, I'm not claiming that this isn't the only crisis we're facing, far from it. What I want to do, in fact, is talk about how the meaning crisis is interacting with other crises, the environmental crisis, the socioeconomic crisis. But in addition to those which are quite well discussed,
cues.zh: 这个核心观点就是，我们的文化正经历着一场深刻的意义危机。接下来，我们必须探讨这个“意义”到底是指什么。我并不是说这是我们面临的唯一危机，远非如此。事实上，我想探讨的是这场意义危机是如何与其他危机相互交织的，比如环境危机和社会经济危机。但在这些已被大众广泛讨论的危机之外，

cues.en: and the public at large, there is a meaning crisis, which is being discussed quite significantly with academia, but needs to be brought to the public at large. Because one of the things I'm going to argue is that these three crises are not independent from each other. They're interdependent in important ways. But what is this meaning that's come into crisis? Why do we hunger for it? How do we cultivate the wisdom
cues.zh: 还存在着一场意义危机。学术界对它进行了相当深入的探讨，但它也需要被带到大众的视野中。因为我要论证的观点之一就是，这三重危机并非彼此割裂。它们在很多重要层面上都是相互交织的。但是，陷入危机的这个“意义”究竟是什么？我们为何对它如此渴望？我们又该如何培养智慧，

cues.en: Because that's what I'm going to argue wisdom is ultimately about, to generate, enhance this meaning. Wisdom is about realizing, in both senses of the word, becoming aware and making real. Wisdom is about realizing meaning in life in a profound way. How do we cultivate this wisdom? What does it mean? And I'm not going to talk about that just practically. I'm going to talk, I mean not just theoretically, I'm going to talk about that practically as well. What are some practices that people can engage in and are engaging in?
cues.zh: 因为我要阐述的正是，智慧的终极追求就是去创造并深化这种意义。智慧在于“领悟”（realizing）——包含这个词的双重含义：既是察觉感知，也是将其化为现实。智慧在于以一种深刻的方式，领悟并实现生命的意义。我们该如何培养这种智慧？它究竟意味着什么？我不仅要从理论层面来谈，还要落实到实践层面。人们可以践行、并且正在践行的方法又有哪些？

cues.en: to try and address this need for the cultivation of wisdom. What role, for example, do mindfulness practices play within the cultivation of wisdom? So, here's the three questions that we're going to keep coming back to again and again and again. What is this meaning? Why do we hunger for it? And how do we cultivate the wisdom to realize it? So, some of the topics, of course, we're going to be addressing are, centrally, the meaning crisis,
cues.zh: 去设法解决培养智慧的需求。比如，正念练习在智慧的培养中扮演了什么角色？这里有三个我们会一再反复探讨的问题：这种意义到底是什么？我们为何渴望它？我们又该如何培养智慧来实现它？当然，我们要探讨的核心议题之一，就是意义危机，

cues.en: How did this kind of meaning evolve? What is it? Why is it so important to the evolution of our humanity? More specifically, the history of the meaning crisis. Why did it arise? What are the historical factors? By doing that, we'll get a historical account of meaning. We'll get a sense of what this meaning is that has come into crisis that people individually feel they are lacking or losing in their lives.
cues.zh: 这种意义是如何演变而来的？它究竟是什么？为什么它对人类的演进如此重要？更具体地说，是意义危机的历史。它是如何产生的？有哪些历史因素？通过探讨这些，我们将理清意义的历史脉络。我们会理解，这种陷入危机、让人们在各自生活中感到匮乏或正在失去的意义，究竟是什么。

cues.en: We want to talk about connections between meaning, wisdom, and, importantly, self-transcendence. It's going to turn out that this notion of self-transcendence, again, which we'll have to develop and explicate, is something that's a core need because it performs core functions for human beings. It's bound up with these ideas of wisdom and, of course, meaning. And along the way, in fact, right from the beginning, we're going to start to see that there's deep connections between meaning, wisdom, self-transcendence, and
cues.zh: 我们要探讨意义、智慧，以及至关重要的自我超越之间的联系。事实证明，这种自我超越的概念——我们随后会对此展开阐述——是一种核心需求，因为它对人类起到了核心功能作用。它与智慧的概念紧密相连，当然，也与意义息息相关。在这整个过程中，其实从一开始我们就会发现，意义、智慧、自我超越，以及

cues.en: altered states of consciousness. Why do human beings seek to alter their consciousness? In fact, not just human beings, other intelligent organisms seek to do this. Right? Caledonian crows will tumble down roofs in order to make themselves dizzy for no other purpose than to alter their state of consciousness. What is going on? Why does intelligence need
cues.zh: 改变的意识状态之间存在着深刻的关联。为什么人类会试图改变自己的意识？事实上，不仅是人类，其他具有智慧的生物也会这么做，对吧？新喀里多尼亚乌鸦会顺着屋顶翻滚让自己眩晕，除了改变自身的意识状态之外没有任何其他目的。这到底是怎么回事？为什么智慧需要

cues.en: to be conjoined to an altered state of consciousness and why in particular have human beings developed very sophisticated processes for generating, harnessing, and interpreting these altered states of consciousness. We're going to talk about that in connection with shamanism and ritual. We're going to talk about that in connection to the flow state. This is when you're in the zone and why people seek it and why it's so powerful. We're going to talk about it, as I mentioned, in connection with psychedelic experiences.
cues.zh: 与改变的意识状态相结合？尤其是，为什么人类发展出了极其复杂的流程，来产生、利用并解读这些改变的意识状态？我们将结合萨满教和仪式来探讨这一点。我们还将结合心流状态来探讨这一点，也就是当你全神贯注、“进入状态”的时候，人们为什么追求它，为什么它如此强大。正如我提到的，我们还会结合迷幻体验来探讨这一现象。

cues.en: More importantly, the mystical experiences that can occur within some psychedelic experience, because it turns out it's the mystical experience that is more important and transformative. But there's a subset of those mystical experiences that are very crucial. These are awakening experiences. These are experiences in which people come back from the mystical experience and say, that was somehow more real than this, and I need to change my world.
cues.zh: 更重要的是在某些致幻体验中可能出现的神秘体验，因为事实证明，神秘体验往往更加重要，也更具转化力量。但在这些神秘体验中，有一个子集至关重要，那就是觉醒体验。在这些体验中，人们从神秘体验归来后会说：那不知为何比眼前的一切更真实，我必须改变我的世界。

cues.en: I need to change myself. They engage in what L.A. Paul has called a transformative experience, what is also known as quantum change, a radical transformation of their lives. And we know, we've got good research now showing that they're right. Their lives get better after these awakening experiences. We're going to talk about that in depth. And dare I say it, maybe we can bring all of this together and actually propose
cues.zh: 我必须改变我自己。他们投身于 L.A. Paul 所说的转化性体验，也就是人们所熟知的“量子飞跃式改变”，即一种对人生的彻底重塑。而且我们知道，现有的大量严谨研究表明他们是对的，经历这些觉醒体验后，他们的人生确实变好了。我们稍后会深入探讨这一点。我甚至斗胆设想，也许我们能把所有这些融会贯通，并真正提出——

cues.en: and maybe some people will be affronted by this, but propose a scientific, a cognitive scientific account of what enlightenment is and why it alleviates the suffering from lack of meaning that is particularly pertinent for us today but has always been a perennial threat since the Axial Revolution. Now that means, of course, we're going to have to also talk about topics that have connection with
cues.zh: 也许有些人会对此感到冒犯——但我们要提出一套科学的、认知科学层面的解释，去阐明什么是开悟，以及它为何能缓解因意义缺失而带来的痛苦；这种痛苦在当下对我们尤为切身，但其实自轴心时代变革以来，就一直是一道长盛不衰的威胁。当然，这也意味着我们还得去探讨一些与此相关的课题，
